messages:
alex kim: quick question — should the SDK start emitting an `x-client-consent` header for user-level telemetry preferences? thinking: `explicit`, `implicit`, `optout` so server can decide routing & redaction preview in console.

mira rao: +1 for a simple header. can we keep values terse? `explicit/implicit/none` maybe. ops-wise we need to know if we can keep sampling for implicit.

samir patel: why does this need to be a header vs a field in the request body? headers are easier for gateways/ingress routing. also: SDK change is smaller.

jen taylor: agree w/ samir. header also lets us route before parsing payload (fast path). downside: some customers proxy-strip custom headers — doc + SDK fallback to body field.

alex kim: proposal: SDK emits `x-rw-consent: explicit|implicit|none`. gateway checks header first, if absent fallback to `client.consent` in body. update console to show a redaction-preview when consent==explicit, and a minimal preview for implicit (PII masked, but we keep coarse telemetry).

mira rao: UX question: preview that shows redaction diffs — we need to avoid showing raw PII in console even to admins unless audit mode is on. so the preview must be itself redacted and show a diff summary. e.g., "3 fields masked (emails, ssn)" and a synthetic obfuscated snippet.

samir patel: on telemetry & quota: if consent==explicit we can keep sampled request/response pairs for quality at 0.1% by default. implicit => drop bodies but keep aggregated metrics. none => no request bodies stored; only counters. this needs to be configurable per-tenant.

jen taylor: routing policy implication: some customers want explicit-consent traffic to stay in private/dedicated environments. we shouldn't hard-route by default, but add a policy rule: `prefer_private_if_consent==explicit`. ops: is that feasible?

ops-bot: infra note: prefer_private rules increase tail placement complexity; will add ~150ms to scheduling decision if we consult placement table. we can cache decisions per 10s to mitigate.

alex kim: good to know. alternative: mark request with `consent_level` for routing filters later, but not mandatory for immediate placement.

mira rao: console feature: add a toggle "Redaction preview (safe)" with tooltip: "Shows a redacted sample and counts of masked values. No raw PII is displayed without audit grant." link to policy.

samir patel: rollout plan: SDK + gateway header support -> beta flag in console (10% tenants) with preview off by default. enable preview for a few internal customers to vet. metrics: sample retention, preview UI clicks, and route cache miss.

jen taylor: small implementation note — header name should be short to avoid proxies truncating: `x-rw-cnsnt`. map in SDK to human-readable in console.

alex kim: ok action items: 1) samir: add header support + fallback to body (PR by EOD Thu). 2) mira: design copy + preview mockups (Mon). 3) jen: add routing policy flag in placement service + cache design (spec Wed). 4) ops-bot: estimate perf impact and recommend cache TTL (this week).

deploy-bot: canary: gateway change v2.14 deployed to canary - 2 instances.

jen taylor: one more: add telemetry tag `consent_level` to all metrics (counter labels) so we can measure opt-in rates without storing PII.

mira rao: sounds good. adding privacy review with legal before we enable preview for customers.

alex kim: thanks all — logging these in the RFC thread. will follow up with PR links here. :thumbsup:
